name: Baby Light: Red Night Light
desc:
Turn your phone or tablet into a warm red night light made for babies — and for the parents who are awake at 2 AM with them.

Bright white and blue light tells the brain "it's daytime." Baby Light floods your screen with deep red and amber light instead, so you can see during night feeds, diaper changes and quick check-ins without the harsh glare that snaps you — and your baby — wide awake.

No ads. No sign-up. No sounds you didn't ask for. Open it, and the room glows.

— THE SCIENCE, SIMPLY —
Light is the strongest signal your body uses to tell day from night. Special receptors in the eye are most sensitive to blue light (around 480 nm) — the kind in white phone screens and ceiling lights. In the evening, that blue light can suppress melatonin, the hormone that helps us feel sleepy.

Red and amber light sit at the far end of the spectrum (roughly 600–700 nm). Research in adults shows these longer wavelengths have far less effect on those receptors and on melatonin than blue or white light does. It's why submarines, aircraft cockpits, observatories and many hospital units switch to red light at night — and why a red glow is a gentler choice for a midnight feed than flipping on the lamp.

Baby Light can't promise your baby will sleep through the night (no app can!). What it does is give you just enough light to do what you need to do — without blasting the room with the most alerting kind of light at the worst possible time.

— WHAT YOU GET —
Four sleep-friendly light modes

How does it work?
Use your finger or shake your phone to open the cap of the metal lighter. When the top lid is open, strike the flint wheel the same way you would with a real cigarette lighter. Sparks will appear under the flint and should light the wick. As this is a very realistic simulator, it is possible that you may not manage to light it on the first try. Keep spinning the flint wheel until the flame appears (or enable the "Always light the flame on the first try" option in settings). When the lighter is on, your phone’s torch will turn on for a better visual effect. You can now move or tilt your phone and observe how the flame reacts. To stop the flame, close the top lid using your finger or by shaking the phone. You can also blow towards the flame (to enable this feature, turn on "Blow to put out the flame" in settings).

name: AirFind: Find Lost Earbuds
desc:
Find your lost Bluetooth devices in seconds.

AirFind scans the Bluetooth around you and lists what it hears, closest first. Follow the live distance and signal strength to walk straight to your AirPods, headphones, speaker, tracker or anything else that broadcasts.

Open a device to get a proximity ring that fills as you close in, plus optional sound and vibration that speed up as the signal strengthens — a hot-and-cold game you can play with the phone in your hand. The last spot where a device answered is saved on a map, so you know which room or which street to start from.

AirFind also surfaces unknown trackers around you, which helps if you want to check whether something you do not recognise is travelling with you.

What it can and cannot do: AirFind reads Bluetooth Low Energy advertisements. Accessories already connected to another phone or laptop usually stop broadcasting, and distance is estimated from signal strength, so walls, doors and even your own body change the reading. AirFind cannot ring, control or unlock someone else's device.

Paid access: unlimited scanning, live distance and last-seen locations may require an active AirFind Pro subscription. Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled and can be managed in your Apple ID account settings.

Metal Detector is an iOS application that detects the presence of metal nearby by measuring the magnetic field value. This useful tool uses the magnetic sensor built into your mobile device and shows the magnetic field level in μT (microtesla). The magnetic field level (EMF) in nature is about 49 μT (microtesla) or 490 mG (milligauss); 1 μT = 10 mG. If any metal is nearby, the value of the magnetic field will increase. 

The metal detector allows you to identify any metal object in the area because all metals generate a magnetic field whose strength can be measured with this tool. 

The usage is simple: launch this app on your mobile device and move it around. You will see that the magnetic field level shown on the screen is constantly fluctuating. Colorful lines represent the three dimensions and the numbers on top show the value of the magnetic field level (EMF). The chart will increase, and the device will vibrate and make sounds, announcing that the metal is close. You can change the sensitivity of vibration and sound effects in the settings.

A decibel meter is a device which measures sound pressure to determine how intense sounds are, measuring in decibels. Decibels are a logarithmic scale based on the sensitivity of the human ear. Prolonged exposure to sounds over 85 decibels can lead to hearing loss, making measurement of decibel levels important for people who work in noisy environments so that they know when they need to protect their ears.

For a frame of reference, normal conversation occurs between around 40 and 60 decibels, depending on who is talking. A firecracker is about 140 decibels, and a jackhammer runs at around 100 decibels. Musicians, mechanics, construction workers, and other people who work in loud environments can endanger their hearing, especially if they work in environments with explosives, which can generate sound waves intense enough to cause pain and immediate hearing damage. A decibel meter can indicate when sound has reached the danger zone.

Mindfulness is defined as paying attention in the present moment, without judgment. Put another way, Mindfulness is about noticing what is happening around you right now.


How do you practice Mindfulness?
There are many ways to practice mindfulness and bring yourself into the present moment, including meditations, breathing exercises, feeling for sensations and more!
For example, try taking a deep breath in through your nose... And breathe out through your mouth. Congratulations! You just did a Mindfulness exercise. In that moment you paid complete attention to your breath, without any judgments.

name: Speaker Cleaner - Eject Water
desc:
Speaker Cleaner removes water and dust from your iPhone speaker using specially tuned sound waves.

Did your phone get wet? Is the sound muffled?

Speaker Cleaner pushes water trapped in the speaker grille out with sound waves — the most practical way to eject water from your phone.

HOW IT WORKS
The app plays sound in pulses. Each pulse drives the speaker diaphragm outward and ejects water, while the short silence between pulses stops the water from being pulled back in. A steady tone can't do that — it sucks the water back.

THE CLEANING PROGRAM (4 STAGES)
- Pulsed Water Ejection: Short bursts of sound push water out of the grille.
- Resonance Sweep: Scans the frequency band where your speaker vibrates most, loosening stubborn droplets.
- Vibration: Shakes the phone to dislodge whatever is left.
- Waveform Tour: A final pass through four different waveforms.

FEATURES
- Full Clean: Bottom speaker, earpiece, or both — pick what you want to clean.
- Speaker Test: Play each speaker separately and hear which one has a problem.
- Stereo Sound Test: Check left-right balance.
- Manual Mode: Generate a continuous tone at any frequency, with 4 waveforms and amplitude control.
- Decibel Meter: Measure ambient noise in real time — live dB readout, average/min/max and history. Measure the before/after difference.
- Safe to Use: Automatic cycle limits and cooldown periods protect your speaker.
- Step-by-Step Guidance: Speaker selection, volume check and a phone-position guide.

name: Stud Finder - Wall Scanner
desc:
Find studs behind drywall using your iPhone's built-in magnetometer.

This app detects metal fasteners (the screws and nails holding your drywall to wood studs) and helps you locate stud lines behind your wall.

HOW IT WORKS
Your drywall is screwed into wooden studs roughly every 16 inches. This app picks up those screws by reading changes in the magnetic field as you sweep your phone across the wall. Find screws in a vertical line and you've found the stud.

HOW TO USE
Take your case off. Hold your phone flat against the wall. Sweep slowly left and right. When the signal spikes, there's metal nearby. Mark each spike, look for a vertical line of hits, and that's your stud.

Drill a small pilot hole before you mount anything heavy. If the bit hits something solid, you're on the stud. If it punches right through, move an inch and try again. Takes 30 seconds.

WHAT THIS APP CANNOT DO
It detects metal, not wood. If there are no screws or nails in the wall where you're scanning, it won't find anything. It also won't work well through thick plaster, concrete, or tile. And it's not a replacement for a professional stud finder on structural work.

For mounting a TV, hanging shelves, or putting up pictures on normal drywall, it works.

No ads. No nag timers. No interruptions.

PRIVACY
No account. No tracking. No data leaves your phone.

name: PlantNet
desc:
Pl@ntNet is an application that allows you to identify plants simply by photographing them with your smartphone. Very useful when you don't have a botanist on hand!

Pl@ntNet is also a great citizen science project: all the plants you photograph are collected and analysed by scientists around the world to better understand the evolution of plant biodiversity and to better preserve it.

Pl@ntNet allows you to identify and better understand all kinds of plants living in nature: flowering plants, trees, grasses, conifers, ferns, vines, wild salads, cacti (and many more). 

Pl@ntNet can also identify a large number of cultivated plants (in parks and gardens) but this is not its primary purpose. We especially need Pl@ntNet’s users to inventory the wild plants, those that you can observe in nature, but also those that grow on the sidewalks of cities or in the middle of your vegetable garden!

The more visual information you give to Pl@ntNet about the plant you are observing, the more accurate the identification will be. There are indeed many plants that look alike from afar and it is sometimes small details that distinguish two species of the same genus. 

Flowers, fruits and leaves are the most characteristic organs of a species and it is them that should be photographed first. But any other detail can be useful, such as thorns, buds or hair on the stem. A photograph of the whole plant is also very useful information, but it is often not sufficient to allow a reliable identificati

desc:
What is Spirit Level? The spirit level, which is used to calculate the correct plane both vertically and horizontally, is brought to the area specified within the scale lines and serves to measure the accuracy of the plane.
A spirit level, spirit level, or simply scale is an instrument designed to indicate whether a surface is horizontal or vertical. The Spirit Level app is a useful, precise, easy to use and incredibly useful tool for iOS devices.

A conventional level meter has a slightly curved glass tube that is not completely filled with liquid. It usually consists of colored spirit or alcohol with bubbles in the tube. On gentle slopes the bubble moves away from the usually marked center point. The Spirit Level app attempts to emulate a real level meter and displays the data as a real level meter would.

The Spirit Level app also features a bulls-eye level meter, a flat-bottomed circular device with liquid on the surface of a convex glass with a circle at its center. This serves to verify on a plane that tubular scales only do in the direction of the tube. The Spirit Level app attempts to emulate a real bull's-eye level meter and displays the data as a real bulls-eye level meter would.

Where can you use the Spirit Level?

A spirit level is often used in construction, woodwork and photography to verify that the object you are working on is level. When used properly, a spirit level can help you create perfectly neat furniture, hang pictures or objects on the wall, properly

desc:
Amplified Bible

The Amplified Bible (AMP) is an English translation of the Bible produced jointly by The Zondervan Corporation and The Lockman Foundation. The first edition was published in 1965. It is largely a revision of the American Standard Version of 1901, with reference made to various texts in the original languages. It is designed to "amplify" the text by using a system of punctuation and other typographical features to bring out all shades of meaning present in the original texts.

A compass is an instrument used for navigation and orientation that shows direction relative to the geographic cardinal directions (or points). Usually, a diagram called a compass rose shows the directions north, south, east, and west on the compass face as abbreviated initials. When the compass is used, the rose can be aligned with the corresponding geographic directions; for example, the "N" mark on the rose really points northward. Compasses often display markings for angles in degrees in addition to (or sometimes instead of) the rose.
